name: dynamics-triage
description: The dynamics skill's four triage axes for one detected feature: class, disposition, reproducibility, plus the regulated-PII flag (#126).

fields.feature: { id, description, signals: [strings the detector saw], reach: 'n/m pages', evidence }

instructions.question: What kind of dynamic feature is `feature`?
instructions.focus: One primary class. A listing fed by an API is a listing (L); the API is only the class when it renders content with no other shape.

L.what: Listing: a block that lists other pages or items — repeated same-site card groups, rails, teasers, dated cards.

S.what: Search: site search, autocomplete, a results page, a search input or a hosted search vendor.

F.what: Form: any submission — a form tag, a form-less control group, a newsletter or contact form, a form vendor.

M.what: Modal or interactive chrome: overlays, dialogs, lightboxes, tabs, accordions, menus, toggles.

V.what: Media: video or audio players, map embeds, iframes injected at runtime.

T.what: Tag or consent: analytics, tag managers, consent managers, RUM, pixels, chat or review widgets loaded as third-party scripts.

A.what: API, personalisation or settings: first-party XHR that renders content, experimentation, CMS settings objects, geo lookups, app bootstrap.
A.not_for: An API that only feeds a listing, search or form — classify those by their shape.

R.what: Relationship: many-to-many listings keyed by taxonomy (related items by tag or category).

X.what: Auth or commerce: sign-in, account, cart, prices, session-bound features.

I18N.what: Locale: language or region trees, hreflang alternates, language switchers.

CR.what: Client-rendered: slots or whole pages filled after load — placeholders, skeletons, an empty main at load.

D.what: Sheet or data file: copy and settings from spreadsheets or JSON files that are not APIs (placeholders, manifests).

instructions.question: What should the migration do with `feature`?
instructions.focus: Prefer the cheapest disposition that keeps the visible behaviour for a real user of the migrated pages.

rebuild-native.what: Rebuild the behaviour in block or runtime JavaScript with no external data: modal loaders, chrome interactions, accordions, forms, clock strings.

index-backed.what: Feed it from the site's own query index: listings, related rails, search.

data-fed.what: Feed it from data outside the page kept reachable: a same-origin API, a snapshot served from the code bus or a sheet.

embed-passthrough.what: Keep a third-party surface as-is: players, iframes, form services, tags and consent managers, re-authored from live ids.

client-only.what: Pure client compute with no network: calculators, filters, comparisons.

static-snapshot.what: Ship the settled DOM as content, with the reason and the unfreeze condition recorded; also the disposition for 'not decided yet'.

decided-out.what: Cannot or must not exist off-origin: session-bound, regulated capture, no consumer on the migrated pages; links kept, a register row written.

instructions.question: What does `feature` need before it can ship on the new origin?
instructions.focus: Only `self` ships autonomously. Anything that needs an owner's credential, capture, backend or decision is not `self`, however small.

self.what: Nothing outside the repository and the captured content: the migration can ship it alone.

needs-credential.what: A key, token, property id or account the owner must provide (a tag manager container, a consent property, an API key).

needs-human-capture.what: Something only a human session can capture (behind login, a paid flow, a device).

needs-backend.what: A backend or API that must be reachable from the new origin, or a data feed to be provisioned.

needs-business-decision.what: A choice only the site owner can make (keep a player, licence a font, drop a feature).

regulated_pii.instructions: Does `feature` capture regulated personal data — health, financial, identity documents, payment details — through a form or flow?

criteria.true: A form or flow asking for health, financial, identity or payment information.
criteria.false: No data capture, or only contact details for a newsletter or callback.
